final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor provided no new admissible evidence and largely narrowed the claim using the same record already considered. That reframing is useful but it does not cure the core compliance failure. The admissible evidence still shows: aggregate readiness passed and rehearsal had no severity-one incidents; rollout starts at 6% with rollback; the affected immigration services intake segment remains exposed; and there is no approved risk acceptance or proven final disclosure covering that exposure. Under the stated policy, operational controls can reduce deployment risk but do not replace the required disclosure or approved-risk-acceptance condition when the named weak segment remains in scope. That is the distinction between a caveated operational-readiness argument and actual policy compliance. Because the unresolved predicate remains unresolved on the current record, the claim is noncompliant rather than compliant_with_caveats.
remaining_concerns: The immigration services intake segment remains below target on supporting-document checklisting and remains eligible in the initial rollout cohort.
There is no admissible evidence of final launch disclosure explicitly covering the immigration services intake limitation for this named launch use case.
The available risk acceptance is only a draft, has a blank approver line, and does not mention immigration services intake exposure.
Policy requires disclosure or approved risk acceptance when the affected use case remains exposed; staged rollout, rollback, and monitoring do not satisfy that predicate by themselves.
